extracted.intended_audience: authors of science fiction novels seeking editorial/developmental feedback
extracted.subtask_description: A diagnostic reading report intended to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of a science-fiction novel (worldbuilding, characters, plot, style) and recommend next editing steps (developmental and line edits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex worldbuilding
rubrics_metrics.description: You have created a complex world, with an intriguing social dynamic (racism with actual different races) and a rich and complex history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for a world that is rich yet not over-explained; this kind of worldbuilding is key for the kind of sci-fi being written. The report notes the author mostly ‘drops readers into the middle of things’ rather than over-explaining, which is framed as a strength if handled confidently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal exposition / immersion by dropping readers into the middle
rubrics_metrics.description: You explain nearly nothing, simply dropping your readers into the middle of things and letting them fend for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technique requires confidence and a solid grasp of the world; when successful it engages readers and demonstrates mastery of worldbuilding. Implicit guidance: avoid heavy info-dumps; trust reader to infer details from context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization — protagonist (emotional engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Katt is a marvelous creation — smart, resourceful, emotionally open, intensely sympathetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good characterization makes readers feel along with the protagonist (e.g., torn over lovers, terror at being dragged into Tenebrae). Emotional authenticity and sympathy are emphasized as markers of strong characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization — secondary characters and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Francois, Devon, and Ro capture in different ways the quandary of immortals falling in love with shorter-lived creatures; Ro balances kindness, family feeling and greed; Francois has a dark past and a believable battle to overcome it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary characters should have clear, complementary conflicts and believable moral complexity. Balance between light and dark in a character (e.g., Ro) makes them believable; redemption arcs must be plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot: open-ended yet satisfying (series balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crafting a plot that is open-ended enough to make your readers want to keep reading the rest of the trilogy yet complete enough to leave them feeling satisfied by the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report praises achieving both tension for future volumes and a sense of completion. Guidance: plots for multi-book projects must resolve enough to satisfy while leaving intriguing unanswered questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic/relationship plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Making the love between Katt and Francois believable after the way he used her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important to craft believable emotional transitions and reconciliation so reader acceptance of relationship developments feels earned, not forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and voice (character voices and elevated authorial voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your character voices are sharp and believable, and you manage to convey even Katt's more bizarre experiences beautifully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, distinct character voices are crucial. The report highlights effective use of a technique where the writing voice momentarily transcends a character's voice (e.g., in dream sequences or rituals); this is tricky but can enhance prose when done well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of dream sequences/ritual descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your descriptions of her dream sequences, and of the Tenebrae ritual at the end, make good use of allowing your writing voice to momentarily transcend your character's voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such passages should be evocative without losing character perspective; they can be stylistic high points if they elevate rather than break voice consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic cohesion (characters confronting pasts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are exploring the problem of how to either overcome or come to terms with their pasts (Francois's drive for revenge, Dune's bigoted upbringing, whatever with Devon, Katt's struggles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong novel weaves character arcs into a coherent thematic exploration. The report treats thematic depth as an asset that unifies plot and character work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot predictability / twist visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer could see some of the future twists coming (e.g., reproductive plot points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-cluing or predictable setups can reduce suspense; the report notes this as a possible drawback and implies the need to manage foreshadowing and concealment of twists carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency of world rules (continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency with internal rules — e.g., fertility drugs and frequent sex yet Ro not able to get Katt pregnant; humans and Innate' can't impregnate Immortals; reality that her DNA has been altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring biological, social, and magic/science rules are consistent across the manuscript is essential; inconsistencies can undercut credibility unless intentionally explained. Use clues and revealed rules to support plot developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective foreshadowing/planting clues
rubrics_metrics.description: Small details (e.g., Ro's son staring at her belly) function as beautiful hints that support later revelations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good foreshadowing should be subtle and rewarding on reread; the report gives this as a positive example and suggests using such techniques to strengthen plot cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-editing needs: micro-level clarity and dialogue clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no persistent stylistic flaws, but there are small, context-specific adjustments to make (e.g., at the beginning it was hard to tell what Jemmy was saying).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend line-editing to fix local clarity problems, tighten prose, and correct moments where dialogue attribution or phrasing confuses the reader. Line-editing is a separate next step requiring the full manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to read full manuscript for intelligent line-editing
rubrics_metrics.description: To line-edit intelligently, the editor needs to have read the entire manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-level edits should be informed by the whole work's arc and voice; partial reads limit the effectiveness of line edits. Practical recommendation: provide full manuscript for a proper line-edit and discuss scope and cost with the editor.
